name: VolumetricClouds
signature: public sealed class VolumetricClouds : Component, IRenderSync

docs.summary:
Volumetric clouds over the whole scene, with optional flat cloud layers above or below them.

The cloud layer is ray marched through the view at a reduced resolution, taking its density from a coverage map around the camera and eroding its edges with 3D noise, lit from a sun map drawn once a frame or by marching a few steps toward the sun. Everything is scaled up over the scene. The scene's first enabled clouds are drawn, by a `VolumetricCloudsFeature` in the scene's world.
Height of the cloud base above zero, in meters.
How tall the cloud layer is, in meters.
How much of the sky is covered.
How quickly light dims inside the clouds. Higher looks heavier and darker underneath.
Size of the weather pattern in meters, how far apart clusters of clouds are.
How much the detail noise eats into cloud edges.
Size of the detail noise in meters.
How much billowy puffs eat into thin cloud, detail at screen resolution on top of [`Erosion`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.VolumetricClouds~Erosion).
How many puffs fit across twice the layer's thickness.
Wind speed in meters a second.
Compass direction the wind blows toward, in degrees around Y.
Scales the sunlight the clouds receive.
Scales the sky light the clouds receive.
How much of the sky's color the sky light keeps. Lower greys it, so clouds do not turn blue.
How bright the rim around the sun gets when looking through thin cloud toward it.
Beyond about this distance in meters the clouds fade into the sky behind them.
How far the clouds reach around the camera, in meters.

Marches toward the sun for every pixel of cloud instead of reading the sun map, which is drawn once a frame from the same march. Sharper self shadowing from the detail noise, at [`LightSamples`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.VolumetricClouds~LightSamples) extra reads of the coverage and noise per pixel.
Samples taken toward the sun for each pixel of cloud, when [`MarchToSun`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.VolumetricClouds~MarchToSun) is on.

Resolution the clouds are built at before they are scaled up over the scene. With [`TemporalUpscale`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.VolumetricClouds~TemporalUpscale) on, only a quarter of these pixels are drawn each frame.

Draws a quarter of the clouds' pixels each frame, a different one of every 2x2 block in turn, and fills in the rest from earlier frames moved to where the clouds are now. About a quarter of the cost for the same sharpness once settled, a little soft for a few frames after fast camera turns.
Radius of the planet in meters, which curves the cloud layers down toward the horizon.
Tiling noise the clouds and flat layers are built from: R broad gradient noise, G billowy cells, B fine gradient noise, A fine cells. Empty uses the built in one.
Tiling 3D noise that erodes the clouds' edges: R at the base scale, G three times finer. Empty uses the built in one.
How far the wind has carried the clouds, in meters on the XZ plane.
The direction the wind blows toward on the XZ plane.
Called when the object becomes enabled and active. Only called when the GameObject is in a Scene and enabled.
Called when the object becomes disabled or inactive. Only called when the GameObject was in a Scene and becomes disabled.
Called every frame.
